title: $S\mapsto\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ preserves coverings
statement:
Let $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite jointly surjective family of profinite
sets. Then $\{\Spec LC(S_i,\Z)\to\Spec LC(S,\Z)\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering in
$(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$ ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). Since the
coherent topology is generated by such families, $u$
([def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale]) is cover preserving.

proof.text: For each map $S_i\to S$, the induced morphism $\Spec LC(S_i,\Z)\to\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ is a morphism over $\Spec\Z$ by the functorial construction of [def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale]. Both structure morphisms to $\Spec\Z$ are weakly étale by [lem-sfb-lc-weakly-etale], and every morphism over a common base between weakly étale schemes is weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The source and target are affine schemes because they are spectra of rings, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: weakly étale affine morphisms

proof.text: Put $X=\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ and $X_i=\Spec LC(S_i,\Z)$, and denote the given maps by $g_i:S_i\to S$ and their induced spectrum maps by $f_i:X_i\to X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] with $R=\Z$: these spaces have points $(s,\mathfrak p)$, with prime ideal $P_{s,\mathfrak p}=\{h:h(s)\in\mathfrak p\}$. By [def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale], the ring map is $g_i^*:h\mapsto h\circ g_i$. Its inverse image of $P_{s_i,\mathfrak p}$ is $\{h:h(g_i(s_i))\in\mathfrak p\}=P_{g_i(s_i),\mathfrak p}$. Thus $f_i$ sends $(s_i,\mathfrak p)$ to $(g_i(s_i),\mathfrak p)$. Given $(s,\mathfrak p)$, joint surjectivity supplies $i,s_i$ with $g_i(s_i)=s$, proving that the $f_i$ are jointly surjective. Now let $V\subset X$ be any affine open. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], each $f_i$ is affine and $V_i=f_i^{-1}(V)$ is an affine open in $X_i$. The finite family $V_i$ has images with union exactly $V$: every image lies in $V$, and a preimage of any point of $V$ under some $f_i$ belongs to $V_i$. Together with weak étaleness from step 1, this is exactly the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. This also covers $I=\varnothing$, when joint surjectivity forces $S=X=\varnothing$. Every covering sieve on the profinite site contains a finite jointly surjective family by [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Its image sieve contains the pro-étale covering family just proved, so it is covering; hence $u$ is cover preserving.

split_report.summary: Split the covering-preservation lemma into two source-backed steps. The first checks weakly étale affine morphisms using the existing locally-constant weakly étale lemma and stability statement. The second uses the existing closed prime-spectrum homeomorphism to prove joint surjectivity on spectra, then applies the pro-étale covering definition and the coherent topology definition. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves were needed. Second reading: wrote the inverse-image prime calculation and checked the covering condition for every affine open using the existing affine-morphism Mathlib leaf; removed worker-owned tool_uses.
